prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web application concept for Wicker Study Tutor, 1440 × 900 landscape
Primary request: Design the "Study Brief" Tutor page as a credible production UI, not a poster. Tutor is workspace-wide but has been opened from the BCS1520 Statistics course, so it begins with that route-aware lens while remaining able to cross-check every connected source.
Input image: existing Wicker Study Practice page; carry over its exact app shell, warm off-white canvas, left sidebar, Archivo/Archivo Narrow feeling, navy ink, indigo action color, thin full-span rules, corner language and density. Do not copy Practice content.
Composition: persistent existing Wicker left navigation. Main header: "Tutor", a small label "Workspace-wide", a removable indigo-tinted context chip "Focused on BCS1520 · Week 4", and right-side buttons "New conversation" and "History".
Directly under header, show a compact full-width briefing band titled "Before you continue" with three equal ruled columns, not separate floating cards: "Due next · Problem set 1 · Friday", "Attendance · Tutorial required this week", and "Progress · Week 4 material 68% covered". Include a quiet link "Ask about this brief".
Below, one broad conversation area with an assistant welcome that acknowledges context: "You’re looking at Statistics, Week 4. I can explain this material or check it against your schedule, requirements, and other courses." Show four substantive starter rows separated by full-width rules: "Explain confidence intervals from this lecture", "What is required for Friday’s tutorial?", "Make a practice set from Week 4", "I will miss Tuesday. Check the impact across my courses". The last one should be subtly emphasized as the example of a cross-workspace request.
Show one short existing answer preview beneath: title "Friday tutorial requirement", two concise paragraphs, then a collapsed full-width row "Evidence · syllabus, Canvas, timetable" and a quiet action row "Plan around this requirement". No assistant speech bubbles.
At bottom: anchored wide composer with context text "Focused on BCS1520, able to check all courses", plus attachment, scope control, and primary send button.
Visual hierarchy: briefing band is useful but compact and clearly yields to dialogue; it must not resemble the Home dashboard. Full-span internal borders always reach panel edges. Avoid nested card stacks, borders ending inside padding, gradients, glass, heavy shadows, oversized blank areas, and decorative illustration. Keep supplied UI text legible and exact. The screen must clearly communicate a route-aware but workspace-capable academic tutor.
